Draw an opening

Pick Window, Slider, Door or Cut-out, then drag a box on the wall (a click drops a standard size). Drag to move, drag the corner to resize. The 3D view on the right turns to face this wall as you work.

Selected opening

Delete key also removes it.

Openings cut real holes in the 3D walls (glass in windows and sliders, a panel in doors, nothing in a cut-out) and appear on the floor plan and on the new Elevations sheet under Draw site plan.

Controls

Place somethingPick it in the Library on the right, then click the ground where it goes. Hold Shift to place several. Esc cancels.
MoveDrag it. Arrow keys nudge 1 ft (Shift 5 ft).
RotateDrag the orange ring around a selected object, or Q / E for 5° steps, R for 90°.
ResizeWidth, depth and height boxes in the inspector.
Raise off the ground"Floor above grade" in the inspector. Posts appear once it's more than about 4 ft up.
SupportsPick slab, stem wall, wood posts, concrete piers or pilings for a building or deck, with spacing, size and cross-bracing; combine with "Floor above grade" for a raised house.
Design the insideSelect a building and press Interior (or I): drop rooms in, drag and resize them, add doors and windows, add an upper floor, or describe the layout for Claude. "Roofs off" shows the rooms in 3D.
Change the shapeSelect a building: Shape presets (gable, hip, shed, A-frame, L, T, porch…), roof pitch and ridge direction, and Wings for attached masses. Or type what you want, or drop a photo, under "Describe it" and let Claude reshape it.
Site plan"Draw site plan" renders a 2D plan sheet with dimensions and a schedule of everything placed.
CameraDrag empty ground to orbit, scroll or pinch to zoom, right-drag or two fingers to pan. In Plan view, drag pans.
MeasureMeasure tool, then click two ground points. Shows distance, rise and grade.
Paint / ExteriorPaint tool (or P), then click any wall, roof, rail, post or door on a house to recolour or reclad just that element. Scope it to the element, the mass or the whole house; Reset exterior clears it. Per-mass and per-wall overrides are keyed by wing position, so deleting or reordering a wing can move them onto a different wing.
Path piecesLibrary: Walk, Ramp 1:12, Landing, Steps, Boardwalk. Drag a piece's end near another piece's end, a door, a stair foot or the driveway and it snaps on. Double-click an end to continue the route. Shift-drag moves it freely without snapping.
RouteAuto route builds a code-compliant chain of pieces from the driveway to a door. Fix piece applies the first suggested fix to the selected piece.
Accessible routeThe code check reports whether each cabin can be reached from the driveway on walks no steeper than 1:20 and ramps no steeper than 1:12 with landings, 36 in wide, with no stairs.
Select a partWith a house selected, click one of its decks, porches, stairs or ramps again to edit just that part (or Alt-click it any time). Esc goes back to the whole house; clicking empty ground lets go.
Part handlesDrag the centre grip to move the part (1 ft steps; Shift for free), the knob to rotate it (5° steps), and the square on an edge to push or pull that edge. Arrow keys nudge 1 ft (Shift 5 ft), R turns it 90°, Delete removes the part.
RailingsOn a selected deck or porch, click the rail chip on an edge to cycle auto, on and off. Auto puts a guard wherever the floor is more than 30 in above the ground; a red chip means a required guard is switched off. The Railings block in the inspector does the same per edge, or all at once.
Add a pieceClick a + chip on a free edge to hang a deck, porch, stair, ramp or door off it, or to start a connection from there. The same buttons are under Add to this part in the inspector.
ConnectConnect tool (or C): click one end (a deck edge, door, stair foot, path end or the driveway), then the other, and pick Boardwalk, Ramp route, Steps, Bridge or Walk. The accessible-route check tells you whether the connection passes.
Stair connectionsConnect offers Stair when the two ends differ by 7 in or more: one straight run (7 in risers, 11 in treads), or an L-stair with a 4 × 4 ft landing when the space is short. Its top lands flush with the deck or door. In a + chip, Stair → … starts one from that edge; click where it should land. Stair pieces also snap their top onto deck edges and doors.
Levels & junctionsSelect a house to see its floor level, each porch and deck surface, and every piece that meets its edges. Fix sets that piece end to the surface it meets; Level everything fixes them all in one undo step. The code check row Level floors & thresholds names any step, and a chip such as 6 in step marks it in 3D.
FlushTwo walking surfaces count as flush when they are within ½ in (13 mm) of each other. Anything more is a step: a trip hazard, and it breaks the accessible route.
Remove / undoDelete removes, Ctrl+Z undoes.

Rivera-Liu compound · schemes

Three placement + building studies for the Architecture #2 brief. Load one, then move, reshape, or open Interior on any building. Each is a starting point, not an answer.

Program budget

Enclosed total0 / 1,600 sq ft
Covered outdoor0 sq ft

Enclosed counts every floor of the main mass plus closed wings; open (porch) wings count as covered. Each building must stay at or below 800 sq ft.

Route

Lays walk, ramp, landing and stair pieces from the driveway to a door: walks up to 1:20, ramps up to 1:12 with 5 ft landings top, bottom and every 30 in of rise, a 1:12 switchback on steeper ground (or stairs), and a dogleg around buildings and ponds.

Code check · SJCC 18.50.540

Live against the current layout. Lot-width rule: structures may cover at most 50 % of the lot width measured through the most seaward point of the primary structure (40 ft if the lot is under 80 ft wide there); decks and porches over 30 in tall count; stairs, ramps and paths do not. Residential height limit 35 ft above average grade. Guards and handrails follow the IRC as adopted in Washington (WAC 51-51): a guard at least 36 in high, with openings that won't pass a 4 in sphere, on any open side of a porch or deck more than 30 in above the ground; a 34–38 in handrail on stairs with four or more risers and on ramps rising more than 6 in. Rails are added automatically where required; set a wing's Rail to on or off to override. In the aesthetic buffer only paths, stairs, ramps and structures under 30 in are allowed. Accessible route (ADA 2010 §402–405 / ICC A117.1 §403–405): walks no steeper than 1:20, ramps no steeper than 1:12 with at most 30 in of rise per run, 60 in landings at the top, bottom and every turn, handrails on both sides of any ramp rising more than 6 in, 36 in clear width, cross slope no more than 1:48, and no steps anywhere on the route.

Site notes · assumptions

Bank: listed as low-bank, but the 2 m USGS surface rises ~14 ft in the first 50 ft inland on the east shore (≈28 % slope) before flattening, so a top of bank ~45 ft in is assumed there; the south-west edge rises gently (≈8 %) so the setback is measured from the water. Verify on site. Madrones: drawn as mature trees (~20 in trunk, 24 ft canopy); keep piers outside a root zone of 1 ft radius per inch of trunk (~20 ft). Wind: San Juan Islands pattern — winter storms from the south-east and south (straight up Mud Bay), summer afternoon north-westerlies; pull Friday Harbor (KFHR) data for the site-analysis sheet. Sun: noon altitude ≈18° at the winter solstice, ≈65° in June; a 3.5–4 ft overhang over 8 ft glass shades summer and admits winter sun.

Setbacks
Shoreline setback from top of bank35 ft
Top of bank, in from the east OHWM45 ft
Side & rear lot lines10 ft

SJCC 18.50.540(C): the aesthetic setback is 50 ft from the top of the bank where screening vegetation exists within 50 ft of the water, otherwise 100 ft; where there is no clear bank it is measured from the OHWM. The USGS surface climbs ~14 ft in the first 50 ft inland on the east shore, so the bank top sits about 45 ft in; the south-west edge is gentle, so it is measured from the water. 18.50.540(C)(6) allows a reduction to 35 ft where neighbouring houses sit closer, which is typical of this low-bank stretch of Islandale Rd — the schemes are sited to that reading (35 ft + 45 ft bank on the east shore, 35 ft from the water on the south-west). Slide to 50 for the strict reading and the inspector shows what moves.

Sources

Parcel boundary: San Juan County assessor via the WDFW statewide parcel service. Elevation: USGS 3DEP 1/9-arc-second LiDAR DEM, sampled every 2 m (6.6 ft), NAVD88. The long wavy edge is the Mud Bay meander line. Tide default is roughly mean higher high water. Dimensions in the library are suggestions; the shed and trailer sizes are guesses at what's there now.
